To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Sn4Sbx5 (x=2,3,4) nanoparticles prepared by microwave assisted co- precipitation technique exhibit the highest electrical conductivity and specific capacity in the range of ~4.54 × 10-4 S.cm-1 and ~153 mAh g-1 respectively.

the microwave treated Sn4Sb4.9 sample exhibits the highest electrical conductivity (4.54 × 10-4 S/cm), diffusion co-efficient of 10-13 cm2 s-11 and specific capacity of 153 mAhg1 for 50 charge-discharge cycles.
the microwave assisted synthesized SnxSby anodes exhibit better electrochemical, electrical properties and reversibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of highly crystalline and electrochemically active tin-antimony based anodic materials for Li ion batteries.
the synthesis and characterization of novel Sn-Sb based alloy anodes and the results obtained are expected to contribute in the field of Li ion batteries.
the synthesis and characterization of Sn-Sb alloy anodes with different elemental composition for Li-ion batteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrochemical properties of SnSb alloy nanoparticles could be improved by the microwave radiation treatment.
, the electrochemical and electrical behavior of the SnxSby compound semiconducting nanoparticles are highly dependent on the elemental composition of the Sn-Sb.
Sn4Sb3 alloy system treated in microwave radiation provides the best anodic material for Li-ion batteries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sn4Sb 5 sample treated in MW radiation provides the best electrochemical and electrical performance among all other compositions.

Sn4Sb3 and Sn4Sb4 samples exhibit better electrochemical properties in aqueous electrolyte and microwave treated Sn4Sb 5 shows better electrical and electrochemical properties in the aqueous as well as the non-aqueous based electrochemical systems.
Sn4Sb3 and Sn4Sb4 nanoparticles treated in microwave radiation would be a better anodic component for Li-ion batteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the SnxSby anodes can be used as anode materials for aqueous Li-ion battery.
the Sn4Sby alloy system treated in microwave radiation exhibits the best electrochemical performance and electrical properties.
the Sn4Sbx5 nanoparticles prepared by co-precipitations and treated in microwave radiation are highly stable, crystalline, and provide high electrical conductivity and specific capacity.
